missing_material_qualifiers: The 82.2% mean is given without noting that per-category success ranges from 94% (rigid) down to 68% (transparent), so a reader could take the mean as uniform performance.
X.trap_note: X never mentions that transparent objects remain weakest at 68%, but it makes no claim of uniformly high success; its 'higher than both baselines across all five categories' is accurate.

Y.trap_note: Y explicitly notes that transparent objects remain challenging at 68% success.
reflexive_qualifiers: Future work should assess whether the gains persist across additional objects, other robots, and longer deployments.

q1_reason: Both texts report accurate numbers (82.2% vs 63.0% vs 46.0%; +11 to +24 over DAgger), but only Y names the remaining gap on transparent objects, which scopes the contribution honestly where X leaves it out.
q2_reason: Y gives all three means, the per-category gain over DAgger and the weakest category, so the overall pattern and its limit are clearer; neither text says that the margin grows on harder categories.
